To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RDDL is suitable to learn representations from signals corrupted by outliers and that it is useful in classification of biomedical signals.

1) RDDL is a novel deep learning tool that learns multiple levels of dictionaries and can learn robust representations from signals that contain heavy tailed outliers, 2) it is more accurate than traditional dictionary learning methods, and 3) it outperforms state-of-the-art deep learning tools on benchmark deep learning data sets.
RDDL yields better results than the state of the art in terms of classification accuracy on benchmark datasets and on the MIT-BIH database.
In summary, our research is concerned with
learning deep features from signals that are corrupted with sparse but heavy tailed outliers.
the problem of learning representations of data corrupted with outliers and noise and with their use for classification.
learning representations for ECG signals that are corrupted with outliers and then use these representations for classifying the arrhythmias in the ECG.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed RDDL method is suitable for learning deep representations from signals with sparse outliers.
